title: fix(plugin-grid): refuse a non-positive `pageSize` at all three read points (objectui#9853)
body:
Part of #9853

⚠️ **`Part of`, not `Fixes`.** Four things survive this merge and are named at the
foot of this body — the card's own direction question is only *partly* closed by
it, the default-value fork triage put in scope is declared but not resolved, the
spec-side half is another repository's, and a fourth site of the same defect
lives in a sibling package outside this fence.

## What this changes

One authored `pagination.pageSize` (or the deprecated flat `pageSize`) reaches
**three** read points in `ObjectGrid.tsx`, and they disagreed about a
non-positive value. All three now go through one resolver, mirroring the
`rowHeight` resolver a few lines above it — *one resolver at every entry is what
keeps the answer single*, which is the shape the filing seat noticed was already
sitting under the defect.

### The three sites, re-derived on the tip this branch was cut from

⚠️ Every line number on the card and on its triage comment was taken on an older
ref, and the tip moved again while this card was being dispatched. Re-derived on
`4b5772299`:

| site | spelling | default | what it did with `0` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| grouped-page seed | `??` | `10` | `0` survives |
| server-window seed | `??` | `50` | `0` survives |
| flat display size | `\|\|` (line-wrapped, the operator sits at the start of the **next** line) | `10` | falls through to `10` |

⭐ **Triage's reading is confirmed in full** — three sites, not two; two seeds,
not one; and the three defaults genuinely are `10 / 10 / 50`.

## ⭐ The reproduction corrects the card in two places

The card was explicit that it had **not** run the real renderer. It has now been
run, over a seven-row / seven-group fixture, and two of its claims do not
survive:

1. **`Infinity` never reaches the screen.** The grouped pager is gated on having
   groups at all, and the run that produces the `Infinity` page count also
   produces zero groups, so the pager never renders. Measured:
   `bodyHasInfinity = false`, no page readout in the document.
2. **The flat table does *not* render normally.** The card says a grid renders
   fine until the author adds `grouping`. It does not: the **server-window seed**
   — triage's third site — sizes the fetch, so `$top: 0` goes out on the wire and
   the grid asks the server for nothing. Measured `$top` values: `[0]`, and a
   plain (ungrouped) grid drew **"No results found"**.

⇒ the defect is **upstream of the grouped pager** and fires with or without
`grouping`. Triage's third site is the primary one, not a footnote.

What the grouped path actually renders with `pagination: { pageSize: 0 }`:

```
groupRows            = 0
$top values          = [0]
bodyHasInfinity      = false
body                 = "Grouped over the first 0 of 7 records. Group counts are
                        page-scoped, and a group whose records all fall beyond
                        the loaded rows is missing here."
```

## ⭐ Why refusing `0` is not this renderer inventing a meaning

The card refused to pick a direction and asked the prior question — *what should
`pageSize: 0` MEAN?* It is **already answered**, in the spec, and the answer is
pinned:

- `@objectstack/spec`'s pagination config declares the member
  `z.number().int().positive().default(25)`.
- Its own suite pins the refusal under the test names **`should reject zero
  pageSize`** and **`should reject negative pageSize`** (with sibling rows for
  `pageSizeOptions`).
- Every other `pageSize` the spec declares is `.min(1)`, each with its own
  `parse({ pageSize: 0 })` → throws pin.
- The `limit` that this block's own `ElementDataSourceMapping` lowers
  `pagination.pageSize` into is declared `.positive()` too.

⇒ `0` is not a spelling whose meaning a consumer may choose. It is a value the
contract refuses, and the renderer was the only party not saying so. This is the
card's option **C**, reached by measurement rather than by preference.

The refusal is **fail-soft on purpose**: throwing would take out the subtree for
a declaration the flat path already tolerated. The value is dropped, the site's
own default is used, and one `console.warn` — on the channel this block already
uses for "you declared it, the renderer dropped it" — names the member and the
value. Negative and non-integer values go the same way; those are the ones the
old `||` spelling passed **straight through** at the flat site, being truthy.

## Ablations — each site separately, and the diagnostic

Every leg mutated the repaired source on disk, proved the mutation landed **by
blob hash** against the `HEAD` blob, ran, then restored and proved the restore by
**hash equality AND an empty `git diff HEAD`**. Absolute paths, `trap … EXIT INT
TERM`; an empty hash is treated as a failure, not a pass.

| ablation | result |
|:--|:--|
| grouped seed → old `??` chain | **RED** — 4 assertions |
| server-window seed → old `??` chain | **RED** — 6 assertions |
| flat site → old `\|\|` chain (first attempt) | ⚠️ **GREEN, 13/13** — see below |
| flat site → old `\|\|` chain (after strengthening) | **RED** — 2 assertions |
| diagnostic conditional inverted | **RED** — 7 assertions, including both silence controls |

⭐ **The green is the finding, and it is reported rather than buried.** The first
flat-site ablation passed everything: for `0` the discarded `||` spelling already
produced the same `10` the resolver produces, so **no assertion written about `0`
can redden that site**. That is exactly the shape triage warned about — a pin
that reddens on two sites and silently tolerates the third. What the two
spellings actually disagree about there is a *truthy invalid* value (`-10 || 10`
is `-10`; `25.5 || 10` is `25.5`), so three rows were added that read the flat
page size off the rendered table through inline data, which is the mount where
that site is the live page size. The ablation then reddens.

## Verification

All heavy runs through the shared lock; VERDICT lines, never a bare `$?`.

| run | VERDICT |
|:--|:--|
| the new pin, on **unmodified** source | `command-exit 1` — **6 failed / 4 passed** (the reproduction) |
| the new pin, after the repair | `command-exit 0` — **13 passed** |
| `packages/plugin-grid/` full suite | `command-exit 0` — **142 files, 1345 tests** |
| `@object-ui/plugin-grid` `type-check` | `command-exit 0` |
| `@object-ui/plugin-grid` `lint` (`eslint .`) | `command-exit 0` — 0 errors, 860 warnings |
| cross-tree files that scan this source | `command-exit 0` — **10 files, 364 tests** |
| `examples/schema-catalog` gallery render | `command-exit 0` |

⚠️ The first `type-check` run reported `Cannot find module '@object-ui/types'`
and friends. That is a **missing prerequisite, not a red gate** — a fresh
worktree has no built workspace `.d.ts`. Recorded because the exit code alone
reads like a failure. After `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-grid^...' build`
the closure resolves and `type-check` is green.

Gates run: `check-changeset-presence` (exit 0), `check:changeset-claims`,
`check:pending-changeset-literals`, `changeset:check`, `check:new-line-citations`,
`check:test-path-roots` — all exit 0. `check:changeset-claims` is report-only and
named four pending bodies quoting `ObjectGrid.tsx`; all four were read and none
is falsified by this diff (they concern locale keys, the relational-meta
pass-through, `exportOptions`, and the bulk-executor dataSource face).

## Cross-tree sweep

Every test anywhere naming `ObjectGrid.tsx` was enumerated and the ones that read
its source text were run (`packages/core`, `packages/types`, `packages/react`,
`scripts`, `apps/console`, `packages/components`, `packages/cli`, `packages/i18n`,
`packages/plugin-view`, `examples/schema-catalog`). objectui#8071's
`object-grid.pagination` pin lives in `apps/console` and is green.

The tree was also swept for the **strings** this diff changes, not for the file
path. Findings are listed below.

## ⛔ What this does NOT do — and why

- **The default fork is declared, not resolved.** The three literals are now
  named constants, so the divergence is a stated choice rather than a by-product
  of three hand-spelled chains that happened to end differently. They are **not**
  collapsed to one number: the same grid with no authored `pagination` shows the
  server-window default per page while it fetches its own rows and the flat
  default when it does not, and picking one changes what *every* undeclared grid
  renders. That is a product decision, and an execution seat inventing it would
  be the same class of move this card exists to stop.
- **No spec change.** Option **B** lands in `objectstack` and is outside this
  fence. Note the relevant asymmetry found while measuring: the *view* arm's
  pagination config is `.positive()`, while the *grid component* arm declares
  `pagination` as `z.unknown()` and `pageSize` as a bare `z.number()`. That gap
  is what lets a refused value reach this renderer at all.
- **The mount-once seed is reported, not changed.** Both seeds are `useState`
  initial values with no syncing effect, so a later schema change does not
  re-seed them — unlike `rowHeight`, which has the effect. Nothing in the ruled
  direction requires changing it, and whether it is deliberate is not this
  seat's to decide.
- **No labels, no readiness, no merge.** Left in **draft** for the seat.
